aspects.says: A transient space hands back the stored object and a persistent one a copy, so a change is made to a clone and written back.
basis: section:12.5 A Transient Space Hands Back the Stored Object, and a Persistent One a Copy

aspects.says: A key holds a list of entries: out appends behind the oldest, push inserts at the head, put replaces them all, and readers get the head.
basis: section:12.1 A Key Holds a Queue: `out` Adds, `put` Replaces, `push` Goes First

aspects.says: An entry nobody takes stays until it is taken, so marks and claims carry a lease.
basis: section:12.2 A Wait Without a Timeout and an Entry Without a Lease Both Last Forever

aspects.says: A listener runs on the writer's thread and does not take the entry: slow work goes to another thread, and a consumer takes with inp and accepts null.
basis: section:12.4 A Listener Runs on the Writer's Thread and Takes Nothing

aspects.says: Each Space operation is atomic but a read followed by a write is not; the two steps go under the space's lock, with outIfEmpty, nextLong or synchronized on the space.
basis: section:12.3 The Space's Own Operations Are Atomic, and a Read Followed by a Write Is Not

aspects.says: A persistent space refuses a value that is not Serializable when it is written, while a transient one accepts it.
basis: section:12.5 A Transient Space Hands Back the Stored Object, and a Persistent One a Copy
aspects.reason: observable only in a real persistent space, which writes files a graded run should not depend on; the lesson shows the error

aspects.says: An in or rd without a timeout waits until an entry arrives, so a consumer loop that uses one cannot be stopped.
basis: section:12.2 A Wait Without a Timeout and an Entry Without a Lease Both Last Forever
